(FINDING_ID: LB_R2_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:952](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L952) and [dynamic_management.py:975](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L975), `_solve_greedy()` deliberately force-assigns tasks even when that means breaking F1 or F3. Then [dynamic_management.py:1005](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1005) reduces those hard-constraint breaches to a warning and still returns a normal `Allocation`, so downstream code can consume a plan the solver already knows is infeasible.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the force-assign path for F1/F3 violations and return a structured infeasible/degraded result, or raise, so callers must decompose, reallocate, or abort instead of dispatching from a known-invalid plan.  
VERIFIED: TRUE)

(FINDING_ID: LB_R2_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34  
DESCRIPTION: `_solve_greedy()` computes `target = _redundancy_target(...)` at [dynamic_management.py:949](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L949), but `_check_feasibility()` only enforces “at least one assignee” at [dynamic_management.py:899](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L899). If a critical task receives 1 of 3 intended replicas because of capacity pressure, the allocation still comes back as feasible. Redundancy is therefore a non-binding hint, not an enforced constraint.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit feasibility check `matrix[j].sum() >= r(t_j)` and surface shortfalls as degraded/infeasible rather than normal success.  
VERIFIED: TRUE)

(FINDING_ID: LB_R2_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.31  
DESCRIPTION: `_redundancy_target()` uses total `K = len(self.models)` at [dynamic_management.py:825](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L825), while `_admissibility_mask()` excludes PM from standard tasks when `K > 1` at [dynamic_management.py:814](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L814). That makes critical-task redundancy intrinsically unattainable in a normal `PM + workers` pool: with `PM + COL + PAR`, the target is 3, but only 2 models are allowed to carry the task.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base `r(t_j)` on admissible load-bearing models for that task, or clamp the target to the admissible count and document whether PM can ever participate in emergency coverage.  
VERIFIED: TRUE)

(FINDING_ID: LB_R2_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42  
DESCRIPTION: Standard tasks exclude PM from service, but `_objective()` and `_balanced()` compute load fractions and variance across all models at [dynamic_management.py:859](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L859) and [dynamic_management.py:919](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L919). An idle PM therefore contributes a fixed zero fraction, inflating variance and making an evenly split worker allocation look imbalanced. The reported `cost/balanced` signal is biased against the architecture the class itself enforces.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute balance and bottleneck only over models admissible for standard task execution, or define a separate coordinator-load term instead of treating PM idleness as worker imbalance.  
VERIFIED: TRUE)

(FINDING_ID: LB_R2_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: The stated objective `J(A)` includes monetary cost, latency bottleneck, and balance at [dynamic_management.py:837](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L837), but candidate selection in `_solve_greedy()` sorts only by current load fraction at [dynamic_management.py:958](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L958). When fractions tie, input order decides; expensive or slow models can be chosen over cheaper or faster admissible alternatives with no construction-time penalty. The solver reports an objective it is not actually optimizing.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rank each tentative assignment by marginal delta in `J(A)`, or at minimum use weighted `c_m` and `tau_m` as tie-breakers after load fraction.  
VERIFIED: TRUE)

(FINDING_ID: LB_R2_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.27  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_k1()` claims to validate both `A(t_j) = {m1}` and `sum b_j <= L1` at [dynamic_management.py:1080](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1080), but the implementation only checks that each task was assigned to the sole model after `solve()` at [dynamic_management.py:1091](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1091). Because `solve()` force-assigns even when overloaded, this validator would still pass an over-capacity K=1 case and give false confidence in the reduction property.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In the validation path, explicitly check `sum(token_demand) <= L1` and require `_check_feasibility()` to return no violations before returning `True`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE)
